newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dollar climbs, European stocks consolidate.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dollar climbs, European stocks consolidate.

text.p: The dollar soared against most major currencies on Thursday after Germany's central bank left interest rates steady at its last meeting before a summer recess.
The U.S. currency was at a six-year high against the mark and 43-month peak versus the Swiss franc. It also reached its highest level this year against the French franc.

"Obviously, there was a contingent out there that, number one, was afraid they (the Bundesbank) might move to variable-rate repos (repurchase rate agreements, used to control short-term interest rates) and number two, that they might make some sort of forex statement, and neither of them happened," said Ben Strauss, assistant vice president at Bank Julius Baer and Co in New York.
European stock markets, pausing to consolidate recent record highs, were overshadowed by the dollar's steady rise.
Finnish FOX index was the exception among stocks, jumping to an all-time peak earlier in the session after telecoms group Ericsson reported strong second-quarter earnings.
Ericsson surged about 12 percent on impressive first-half results. Ericsson said pre-tax profits gained 44 percent versus a year ago.

Germany's DAX index, Europe's forerunner in the race this week to all-time highs, ignored the Bundesbank's rate decision and closed bourse trading sharply lower. The DAX was weighed down by banking shares, which fell on corporate earnings.
Commerzbank AG and Vereinsbank AG fell after first-half results. Commerzbank ended down three marks at 62.00 despite higher-than-expected first-half operating profits, which rose 23.2 percent.
Vereinsbank shares closed down 12.50 marks at 102.50 on lower-than-expected earnings. Its operating profit rose 15.2 percent in the first half.

Despite the DAX's slip, traders remained upbeat on the index, saying the dollar's continued strength and money pouring into the market should keep the index buoyed. The strong dollar helps make German goods cheaper abroad, which should boost exports.
Dutch shares, which also posted a record high on Wednesday, lost ground by midday despite an earlier boost from Philips Electronics NV's strong second-quarter earnings.

Philips shares jumped more than eight percent to a year high of 177 guilders ($86.16) after the company said second-quarter net profits from ordinary operations rose to 693 million guilders, outpacing analysts' expectations between 429 and 540 million.

French stocks recovered early losses made when investors sold shares to lock in profits made in this week's jump to record highs. But the gains were pared when the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped into negative territory shortly after the open.
After an hour of trading, the Dow was down 29.73 points at 8,058.63.

The Dow's drop also dragged London's FTSE-100 index lower. The FTSE had gained earlier on a smaller-than-expected British May trade deficit. The deficit tallied 508 million sterling ($851.2 million), sharply lower than April's 989 million and forecasts for 960 million.
Imperial Chemical Industries Plc was down 14 pence at 911 in mid-afternoon after first-half profits fell to 160 million sterling from 367 million last year, as expected.
CURRENCIES AT 1540 GMT
The dollar was at 1.8335 marks and 115.97 yen compared to 1.8235 and 115.73 in late trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1540 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 0.3 point at 4,874.2.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index ended bourse trading down 70.35 points, or 1.6 percent, at 4,335.74.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 7.01 points at 2,996.52.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in London at $321.95 per ounce in the afternoon from the morning's $321.80. Silver was fixed at $4.31.
($ = 2.054 Dutch Guilders)
($ = 0.596 British Pounds Sterling)
